headline: Civil Rights History and Black Belt Heritage in Selma
reservation: No city-wide entry permit is required for Selma, but group tours for historic sites should be coordinated in advance. Certain museums and cultural centers have specific operating days that vary seasonally; always consult official websites before arrival. Lodging in the Black Belt region is limited, so confirm reservations well ahead of your visit.

days.title: The Path of the Voting Rights Movement

stops.name: Edmund Pettus Bridge
stops.detail: Walk across this National Historic Landmark, the site of the 1965 Bloody Sunday conflict and a pivotal symbol of the Civil Rights Movement.

stops.name: Brown Chapel AME Church
stops.detail: Visit the headquarters for the Selma voting rights campaign and the starting point for the Selma to Montgomery marches.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes for local transfers; conditions vary
days.note: The bridge is an active U.S. Highway 80 route; use the designated pedestrian walkways only.

days.title: Old Town Architecture and River History
days.start: Suggested: 10 AM from Old Town Selma

stops.name: Old Live Oak Cemetery
stops.detail: Explore the grounds known for Spanish moss-draped oaks and the monuments of prominent figures from Alabama history.

stops.name: Sturdivant Hall
stops.detail: Tour one of the South's best-preserved Greek Revival mansions to understand the antebellum era of the region.

days.note: Walking paths in the cemetery can be uneven; sturdy footwear is recommended.

days.title: Black Belt Natural Landscapes

stops.name: Selma Interpretive Center
stops.detail: Engage with exhibits that provide context for the National Historic Trail before heading toward Lowndesboro.

stops.name: Alabama River Access
stops.detail: View the river bluffs that defined Selma's early role as a cotton shipping port and strategic military site.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for regional loop; conditions vary
days.note: Interpretive centers may have reduced hours on federal holidays; verify before departing.

intel.title: Downtown Hubs
intel.text: Street parking is generally available near the Selma Interpretive Center and along Water Avenue. Large vehicle parking is situated near the riverfront parks.

intel.title: Black Belt Coverage
intel.text: Expect consistent signal in Selma, but be prepared for intermittent service when traveling rural routes like Highway 80 toward Montgomery. Offline navigation is useful for finding specific trail markers.

intel.title: Regional Services
intel.text: Major fuel stations are located along the Broad Street corridor. Services become less frequent in the rural stretches of the Black Belt, so plan accordingly.

intel.title: Seasonal Humidity
intel.text: Spring offers blooming azaleas and temperate weather, whereas late summer brings significant humidity and heat. Schedule outdoor walking tours for early morning.

intel.title: Historic District Navigation
intel.text: Many historic sites are located within a walkable radius, but some transition into residential areas. Respect private property boundaries when viewing historic homes.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental at Montgomery Regional Airport and take US-80 West; Selma is approximately an hour's drive through the scenic Black Belt region.
plan.vehicle: Standard passenger cars are ideal for Selma's city streets; no specialized off-road vehicle is required for this itinerary.
plan.goldenHour: The banks of the Alabama River near the Edmund Pettus Bridge for sunset silhouettes of the steel arches.
